title: WireGuard preset rebinds lnd admin REST API to 0.0.0.0 as a side effect of enabling lndconnect
description: Importing the wireguard preset together with services.lnd.lndconnect.enable sets services.lnd.restAddress = "0.0.0.0" and tor.enforce = false. The macaroon-admin REST endpoint (withdraw-capable with the admin macaroon) then listens on all interfaces, protected solely by the NixOS firewall default-deny plus a subnet-scoped accept rule. The preset does not assert networking.firewall.enable, so any deployment where the firewall is off (user-disabled, or container deployments via extra-container where the in-container firewall is typically disabled) silently exposes the admin API to the LAN/WAN. This is the exact M-2 pattern the fork fixed in lndconnect.nix, reintroduced through a preset, and it contradicts lndconnect.nix's documented invariant that 'enabling lndconnect never changes the listen address implicitly'.
recommendation: Bind restAddress to the WireGuard server address ("${wgSubnet}.1") instead of 0.0.0.0, with the lnd unit ordered after wireguard-wg-nb.service so the address exists at bind time. If 0.0.0.0 is kept, add an assertion on networking.firewall.enable and update the lndconnect option doc to disclose the preset's rebind.
exploit_condition: Firewall disabled or non-enforcing environment (e.g. NixOS container) plus network attacker able to reach the host; still requires a macaroon for full compromise, but unauthenticated DoS and probing surface is exposed.

title: Inverted dirty-tree guard: check fires when -f is given, not when it is absent
description: The guard reads `if [[ $forceRun ]] && ! git diff --quiet ../flake.{nix,lock}`. This errors out when -f IS passed and the tree is dirty, and silently proceeds to overwrite flake.nix/flake.lock when the tree is dirty WITHOUT -f. The intended safety check (refuse to clobber uncommitted pin changes unless forced) is exactly backwards. Maintainer-facing tool, so impact is accidental loss of uncommitted pin work, not a deployed-node vulnerability.

title: netns-exec execs target with caller's full environment
description: After the M-6 fix the wrapper requires an absolute path and drops caps, but execv still inherits LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH etc. into the binary executed inside the service netns. The source comment correctly notes the only allowed invoker (operator, 0500 owner-only file-cap wrapper) is already root-equivalent via NOPASSWD sudo/doas to the service users, so there is no privilege boundary crossed. Recorded for completeness; no action required.
recommendation: Optional: exec with a scrubbed environment if the wrapper's allowed-user set is ever broadened.

title: Dead code: mkCliExec / cliExec wiring unused
description: mkCliExec is defined but never referenced, and the cliExec option keeps its default "exec" with no consumers. Harmless, but dead indirection in a security-sensitive module invites confusion about how operator CLI-in-netns is actually performed (it is netns-exec directly).
recommendation: Delete mkCliExec and the cliExec option, or wire them up.

title: Stale nixpkgs-25_05 input is threaded through pinned.nix but unused
description: The locked nixpkgs-25_05 is from 2026-01-01 while stable/unstable pins are from 2026-08-19/22. helper/update-flake.nix's version-selection logic only compares stable vs unstable; pkgs-25_05 is passed into pinned.nix and re-exported but never selects a package. No security impact today, but a stale input that looks like a pin baseline is a maintenance hazard.
recommendation: Drop the nixpkgs-25_05 input and the pkgs-25_05 parameter, or resume using it deliberately.

title: Committed demo SSH private key
description: id-vm is a real private key in the repo, used by deploy-krops.sh / deploy-qemu-vm.sh with StrictHostKeyChecking=no. Scripts carry prominent 'MAKE SURE TO REPLACE' warnings and the key only grants access to throwaway local demo VMs. Risk is a user copying the demo into production unchanged.
recommendation: Keep as-is, or generate the key at demo start to remove the temptation entirely.

title: All shipped components at versions with no known applicable advisories
description: bitcoind 31.1, lnd 0.21.2-beta, btcpayserver 2.4.2 (the security release; not an RC), electrs 0.11.0, nbxplorer 2.6.10, lndconnect 0.2.1, lndinit 0.1.3-beta. All 2026-08-14 actionable CVE rows are closed by deletion or bump; verified against current tree. nixpkgs stable/unstable pins are 2-5 days old at HEAD.
recommendation: Continue weekly pin automation with the VM suite as gate.

title: HEAD's four onion-hostname/secret-file fixes are correctly implemented
description: Onion content regex anchors the whole string and fails closed on multi-line injection; read-once-into-variable closes the -L/cat TOCTOU as claimed; all chowns use -h; populate-as-root-then-chown ordering leaves no symlink window; electrs.toml written with install -m 600; cookie chmod is an explicit 0640 (and runs as the unprivileged bitcoin user in any case).

title: wireguard preset binds lnd admin REST API to 0.0.0.0, protected only by the firewall
description: When the wireguard preset is enabled with lndconnect, services.lnd.restAddress is set to "0.0.0.0" and tor.enforce = false. The admin-macaroon REST endpoint (full wallet control) therefore listens on every interface, including any public one. Protection is a single NixOS firewall accept rule limited to the wg subnet. If an operator disables networking.firewall.enable (common on trusted-LAN setups) or disrupts rule ordering, the admin endpoint is exposed to the network with no second layer.
impact: Potential exposure of lnd's admin REST API (fund movement, channel control) beyond the WireGuard peer if the firewall is off or misconfigured.
recommendation: Bind restAddress to the wg interface address serverAddress ("${wgSubnet}.1") instead of 0.0.0.0. lndconnect-wg already targets serverAddress, so pairing still works and the endpoint is unreachable from any non-wg interface without depending on the firewall.

title: btcpayserver and nbxplorer silently disable MemoryDenyWriteExecute (W^X)
description: Both .NET daemons set MemoryDenyWriteExecute = false, overriding defaultHardening. This is required for the .NET JIT, but it is an undocumented exception to the audit's 'every daemon gets full defaultHardening' claim, and btcpayserver is the internet-facing service. The weakened W^X policy widens the exploit surface for any RCE in the btcpayserver HTTP request path.
impact: A btcpayserver/nbxplorer code-execution bug can write and execute shellcode in-process, which full W^X would block.
recommendation: Keep the override (it is necessary for .NET) but document it explicitly at the override site and in the security audit doc, alongside a note to re-check if a future .NET runtime supports W^X or AOT compilation. Consider AOT-publishing btcpayserver to re-enable W^X if upstream offers it.

title: onion-addresses content-validation fix (121406c) verified sound
description: The 121406c fix validates copied tor hostname content as exactly one 56-char base32 v3 onion address. Tested the bash ERE ^[a-z2-7]{56}[.]onion$ against every multi-line injection payload (trailing shutdownnotify=, bitcoind.rpchost=, evil-first, bare injection, onion+newline+x): all no-match, because bash's $ anchors to end-of-string without REG_NEWLINE. Read-once-into-$content before validation closes the symlink check-then-read TOCTOU. The config-injection splice path uses the root-owned services/<svc> file, not the user-owned <user>/<svc> file. No residual issue.
impact: None. tor-user -> service-user config injection (the original high finding) is closed.
recommendation: No action. Re-verify the regex if tor onion address length or alphabet ever changes (v3 is 56 base32 chars; a future v4 would need an update).

title: Committed SSH private key in examples/qemu-vm is a disposable test fixture
description: An OpenSSH private key is committed at examples/qemu-vm/id-vm. It is the key for the disposable QEMU test VM, which auto-logs-in as root (services.getty.autologinUser = "root") and authorizes only ./id-vm.pub. It is not a production credential and guards nothing of value.
impact: None. The VM is a local throwaway test environment with root autologin.
recommendation: No action. Optionally add a one-line comment at the key noting it is a public test fixture, so a future scanner or reader does not flag it.
